stem.text: A particle moves along the polar curve \( r = 4 \sin{\left(\theta \right)} + 1 \) so that at time t its angle is \( \theta(t) = \frac{\pi t}{12} \), for \( 0 \le t \le 6 \). Using a calculator, find the time t at which the y-coordinate of the particle's position is 2.6. Show the setup for the calculation, and give the value correct to three decimal places.

worked_solution.text: The coordinate is \( y = r\sin\theta = \left(4 \sin{\left(\theta \right)} + 1\right) \sin{\left(\theta \right)} \), so in terms of time \( y(t) = \left(4 \sin{\left(\frac{\pi t}{12} \right)} + 1\right) \sin{\left(\frac{\pi t}{12} \right)} \).
Solve \( \left(4 \sin{\left(\frac{\pi t}{12} \right)} + 1\right) \sin{\left(\frac{\pi t}{12} \right)} = 2.6 \) on \( 0 \le t \le 6 \) with a calculator. The only solution is \( t \approx 2.913 \).

options.derivation: the equation solved in theta and the angle reported in place of the time
r treated as the y-coordinate, so the time at which r equals the value is reported
the angle rounded to one decimal place before it was converted to a time
